title: LTS Bridge Notice & Changelog Playbook for Customer Upgrades
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Purpose:
This ticket captures the canonical customer-facing playbook for communicating upgrades from a previous stable runtime to runtime-2.4-LTS. It bundles the changelog structure, migration guidance, templated comms (email, in-console banner, release notes), and the rollout gating criteria we will use to protect customers during canaries and phased upgrades.

Audience:
- Customers on hosted API and Dedicated customers with pinned versions
- Customer Success and Solutions Engineering who will manage outreach
- Support and SRE for on-call escalation during rollout

Scope:
- Public changelog format and human-readable migration guide
- Three-tier communication cadence: pre-upgrade notice (30d/14d/7d), launch-day announcement, follow-up post-upgrade summary
- In-console banner copy and API deprecation header guidance
- Automated migration assistant script pointer (upgrade-assistant v0.9) and SDK compatibility notes

Changelog structure (customer-facing):
1) Summary (1-2 sentences)
2) What changed (bulleted non-technical overview)
3) Who is affected (LTS channel subscribers, Dedicated users on runtime < 2.4)
4) Action required (none | recommended | required) with dates
5) Breaking changes (explicit with migration steps)
6) Deprecations and timeline (dates for removal)
7) Rollback and support (how to get help)

Migration guidance (high level):
- Compatibility matrix: runtime-2.4 is compatible with SDKs >= 1.14; older SDKs will see a warning header.
- Migration steps:
  1. Run upgrade-assistant --inspect against a staging tenant to surface deprecated API usages.
  2. Apply suggested prompt-preserving config changes (KV cache path and batch size adjustments).
  3. Run integration tests and measure token latency/throughput delta.
  4. If errors, set runtime pin to previous LTS via Console -> Deployment -> Version Pin.
- Automated helper: https://drive.google.com/file/d/upgrade-assistant-v0.9.zip (internal), and sample CLI: upgrade-assistant --tenant my-tenant --report ./migration-report.json

Message templates (short samples):
- Pre-upgrade email subject: "Upcoming: runtime-2.4-LTS — Important upgrade window and recommended actions"
- Pre-upgrade email body (summary): "Starting 2026-04-15 we will commence platform upgrades to runtime-2.4-LTS. Most customers will see no action required. If you are using custom kernel plugins or SDKs older than 1.14, follow the migration guide linked below."
- In-console banner (short): "Scheduled upgrade to runtime-2.4-LTS on 2026-04-15. See migration guide and run upgrade-assistant."
- Release day push (post): "runtime-2.4-LTS is now rolled out to X% of traffic. Known issues: none. Learn more: [link to changelog]"

Rollout gates and criteria (internal):
- Canary Phase (0-5%): 72-hour stability window; success metrics: error rate <= baseline +0.5pp, 99th percentile token latency <= baseline +40ms, anomaly rate on quality checks <= 0.3%
- Ramp Phase (5-50%): 48-hour sub-windows with automated stop if error rate > baseline +1.0pp or customer P99 latency regression > +80ms
- Broad Release (50-100%): Manual approvals from SRE and PM after successful ramp.
- Automatic rollback triggers: sustained error rate spike for 2 evaluation windows, or a critical customer report with P1 impact.

Support & escalation:
- First line: Support tier (support@redwood.ai) with canned triage template: tenant ID, request-id, observed latency, and recent logs.
- Escalation: On-call SRE (pager) if outage or regression meeting P1 criteria.
- Triage SLA: initial response within 4 hours for P1, 24 hours for P2.

Internal checklist (owners called out):
- PM (Ana Ruiz): sign-off on customer email copy, confirm migration guide link live
- Docs (Priya Nambiar): publish migration guide and changelog page with examples and sample requests
- ENG-Release (owner: Jonah Park): run canary and provide telemetry snapshot, merge runtime-2.4 release PR
- DevEx (owner: Sienna Cole): publish SDK compatibility notes and patch release if needed
- CS Ops (owner: Marco Diaz): prepopulate customer list for targeted outreach (Dedicated customers pinned <2.2)

Compliance and legal notes:
- Any changes that touch guarantees for data residency or export must be reviewed by Security & Legal. For runtime-2.4-LTS, key management behavior is unchanged but a security review is requested as a precaution.

Fallback messaging and rollback guidance for customers:
- If we trigger a rollback for a tenant, CS will send a personalized note: "We've reverted your tenant to runtime-2.3-LTS due to observed regressions. No action needed unless you notice persistent errors; we will follow up with root cause and next steps."

Measurement & success criteria post-upgrade:
- No more than 0.5% customers experience actionable regressions attributable to runtime changes
- Migration-assistant run rate >= 60% of targeted Dedicated customers before upgrade date
- NPS/CSAT signals on release communications >= historical baseline

Retention of artifacts:
- Publish canonical changelog and migration guide under /docs/releases/runtime-2.4-lts on Confluence and pinned Drive folder. All PRs and incidents that relate to the upgrade must reference PM-8561.

Longer-term follow-up items (after release):
- Postmortem for any customer-impacting incidents within 14 days
- Evaluate whether migration-assistant can be surfaced as a console action for Dedicated customers
- Bake migration checks into Redwood Optimize recommendations

Notes on tone and copy: keep comms clear, non-technical where possible, and call out explicit next steps with links. Use bolded dates and action verbs in emails for clarity.
